Convert view return values of str, bytes, dict, list, Response, generator/iterator, or tuples (value, status, headers) into a Response, using the app's JSON provider to serialize dicts.
jsonify builds application/json responses: single dict or kwargs produce an object, multiple positional args produce an array, and mixing args with kwargs raises TypeError.
dumps/dump/loads/load prefer current_app.json provider when an app context exists and fall back to Python's json module otherwise; dump writes UTF-8 text.
htmlsafe_dumps escapes U+2028 and U+2029 so JSON can be embedded in HTML/JS safely.
Requests with media types matching application/*+json are treated as JSON for parsing.
Malformed JSON request bodies result in HTTP 400, with detailed decode errors included only when DEBUG is enabled.

before_request handlers may short-circuit by returning a response; after_request handlers receive and must return the response; teardown_request always runs and receives the exception or None; sync and async variants are supported.
Request and application contexts are pushed and popped automatically around request handling; accessing context proxies outside a context raises clear 'Working outside of ... context' errors.
Application and request lifecycle signals are emitted at the correct times: appcontext_pushed/popped, request_started/finished/tearing_down, and got_request_exception.
The g namespace is created per application context, allows attribute access plus get/pop helpers, and raises clear errors on missing attributes.
Templates load from the app and blueprint locations via a dispatching loader; default context processors inject g and the concrete request, preserving the session proxy.
Template context processors from the app and blueprints are merged into the render context; explicitly passed variables override processor or global values.
Autoescaping is enabled for template names that imply markup (.html, .htm, .xml) following configured rules.
Rendering emits before_render_template (with mutable context) and template_rendered signals; streaming render preserves application context.
Blueprint registration namespaces endpoint names with the blueprint name (and name_prefix), applies url_prefix and url_defaults, and executes deferred record/record_once callbacks.
Blueprints can register lifecycle hooks (before_request, after_request, teardown), error handlers, template filters/globals/tests/context processors scoped to their routes.
A blueprint static route is registered when static_folder is set, serving from the folder relative to root_path and applying send_file max-age configuration.
Static file responses and flask.send_file honor SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT: None produces no timed cache, timedeltas convert to seconds, and per-file overrides are allowed via get_send_file_max_age.
send_file enables direct_passthrough by default for efficient streaming, with the option to disable for full content access; send_static_file accepts path-like objects.
url_for builds external URLs when _external is True and allows overriding the scheme via _scheme; it raises BuildError when an endpoint can't be built and requires SERVER_NAME for external URLs.
url_for requires an active application context; subdomains are included in generated hosts when configured.
Request objects expose the matched url_rule and view_args on success, routing_exception on failure, and valid_methods via routing_exception when the method is invalid.

Request size limits enforce MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH from app config or a per-request override, returning 413 on overflow; defaults are applied outside an app context and infinite streams are not read when size is unknown.
Host validation enforces TRUSTED_HOSTS (exact or dot-prefixed domains), returning 400 for untrusted hosts.
Session cookies are cryptographically signed with SECRET_KEY using a tagged JSON serializer; invalid or expired signatures yield a new empty session.

Sessions write cookies only when modified and delete the cookie when modified to empty; permanent sessions get explicit expiration from app.permanent_session_lifetime and may refresh on each request per configuration.

Session cookies include configurable attributes (name, domain, path, secure, httponly, samesite) and add Vary: Cookie when the session is accessed; in-place mutation of nested values requires marking the session modified.

Error logging writes to the active request's wsgi.errors stream when present, otherwise to sys.stderr; a default stream handler with a fixed format is attached only if no level-capable handler exists.
The app logger is named after the import name, uses DEBUG level when app.debug is True and no explicit level is set, and respects logger propagation when determining handler coverage.
CLI app discovery locates a Flask instance named app or application, or calls a factory named create_app/make_app without arguments; multiple apps raise NoAppException requiring module:name.
CLI loading reports clear UsageError/NoAppException when an app cannot be found or a factory requires unsupported arguments; factories with kwargs are supported where implemented.
The CLI environment loader reads .env files, preserves existing environment variables by default, and prepare_import accepts module import strings or file paths.

CLI command groups (FlaskGroup, AppGroup) organize app-specific commands; with_appcontext ensures commands run inside an application context; ScriptInfo loads the app lazily; version is read from package metadata.
Configuration can load from a Python file, module/object import path, JSON, or TOML (when available), and only uppercase keys are imported.
from_envvar reads a path from an environment variable and loads that file; from_pyfile/from_json honor a silent flag to suppress errors.
from_mapping updates config from a dict or iterable of pairs; get_namespace returns keys with a prefix, optionally stripping the prefix and lowercasing names.
ConfigAttribute descriptors read/write values in app.config and can apply a converter when accessing.
Prefixed environment variable loading imports only keys with the given prefix, strips the prefix, supports type coercion (bool, int, float, list, dict), and maps double underscores to nested keys.
Test request environment building composes a base URL from SERVER_NAME (or localhost), APPLICATION_ROOT, and PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME; subdomain is prepended when provided.
The test builder rejects passing subdomain or url_scheme together with base_url; full URLs in the path override scheme/host and set the request path accordingly.
The test client defaults to REMOTE_ADDR=127.0.0.1 and a Werkzeug User-Agent, accepts a json parameter that serializes data and sets Content-Type, and can take an EnvironBuilder in client.open.
Using the test client as a context manager manages request/app contexts; session_transaction provides a safe context to inspect or modify the session.
Class-based views: as_view wraps a View subclass's dispatch_request, applies class decorators in order, and respects init_every_request (default True).
MethodView dispatches to methods named after HTTP verbs (case-insensitive); GET implies HEAD when no HEAD is defined; unsupported methods return 405 with an Allow header.
Automatic OPTIONS handling lists allowed methods (including HEAD and OPTIONS) unless provide_automatic_options is disabled to allow custom handling.
Error handlers can be registered by exception class or status code; HTTPException instances are treated as normal responses; handlers receive the exception instance.
Invalid error handler registrations are rejected: registering with an exception instance, with a non-Exception type, or with an invalid HTTP status not represented by an HTTPException subclass.

Unhandled exceptions are wrapped as InternalServerError (500) in production (app.testing False), with original_exception available to a 500 handler; abort(500) produces a 500 without an original_exception.
Blueprint-scoped error handlers handle exceptions raised by routes in that blueprint; app-level handlers act as fallback when no blueprint handler matches; more specific handlers override parents.

Async views are supported across function views, blueprints, View subclasses, and MethodView methods; async error handlers can return custom statuses; add_url_rule with as_view works with async classes.
Helpers wrap generator responses with stream_with_context to preserve request/session/g, require headers to be set before streaming starts, and ensure session access occurs before streaming.
safe_join prevents directory traversal when serving files; open_resource reads files relative to app.root_path with text or binary mode options.

The tagged JSON serializer preserves non-standard types (bytes via base64, UUID, datetime as HTTP-date, Markup) and nested containers, and represents mappings needing order or non-string keys as lists of pairs.
JSON tag registration maintains ordered evaluation and a key-to-tag map; registering a duplicate key raises KeyError unless force=True; tags can be inserted at a specific index.
The session serializer uses the tagged JSON mechanism so session data with non-standard types round-trips reliably.

The Flask application acts as a registry for routes and templates, resolves resource paths from the import name (handling packages vs modules), provides a default JSON provider, and uses a standard redirect helper.
Timeout normalization accepts int seconds or timedelta and returns a timedelta; None and already-timedelta values are returned unchanged.
Each Blueprint exposes an AppGroup CLI namespace using its name, enabling grouping of blueprint-specific CLI commands.
Blueprint and application static file handlers compute cache lifetimes using SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT read from app.config, returning None to favor conditional requests when configured.
Debug helpers raise DebugFilesKeyError instead of generic KeyError/BadRequest for missing uploaded files when the request is not multipart, including transmitted filenames in the message.

In debug mode, routing that would drop the request method or body due to a redirect (such as trailing-slash normalization with non-307/308) raises FormDataRoutingRedirect with guidance; production behavior is unchanged.
UnexpectedUnicodeError is raised when unexpected unicode or binary data is encountered, improving diagnostics for encoding mistakes.
Custom URL converters can be registered, implement to_python and to_url (e.g., comma-separated list parsing), and may access request and session for context-aware behavior.
get_db returns a single SQLite connection per request using sqlite3.Row rows, parses declared types, converts 'timestamp' text to datetime, and closes the connection on app context teardown.
A CLI 'init-db' command executes schema.sql to reset tables and prints a confirmation; init_app registers teardown and CLI setup with the app.
Instance path handling requires absolute instance_path values; defaults are derived from the app import location (module, package, or namespace) and normalized to filesystem strings.
